Trailing P/E of 23.65× sits within the IT sector benchmark range of 22–30×, grading FAIR; however, forward P/E of 17.21× falls significantly below the sector lower bound and the EV/EBITDA of 15.15× is at a 35% discount to the broad-market median (23.3×), and with the stock at just 7.4% of its 52-week range (near lows), risk/reward tilts incrementally toward cheap — primary yardstick used is P/E + EV/EBITDA given the IT services capital-light model. The biggest risk is that a 73.9% US revenue concentration faces the active RISK_OFF macro headwind (IT sector macro underweight, rising US yields), while an anomalously high D/E of 9.58× — atypical for an IT peer and possibly inflated by Ind AS 116 leases plus the pending €160M Randstad acquisition — adds balance-sheet uncertainty that is not yet resolved.

Newgen is a mid-cap Indian software product company that sells low-code and AI-led process automation platforms (NewgenONE), mainly to banks, insurers and governments. It is not a headcount-driven services firm. Q2FY27 revenue was ₹422 cr (+5.0% YoY) and PAT was ₹87 cr (+6.0% YoY, 20.6% margin). Headline growth has slowed from +11.2% in Q1FY27, so the pre-computed 'accelerating' label is wrong because the table is ordered newest-first. Underneath, quality is better: annuity revenue grew 15% to ₹268 cr (63.5% of revenue), SaaS grew 36% (down from 40%) and subscription grew 18% (down from 21%), while lumpy licence and implementation revenue dragged the total. On the IT yardstick of trailing P/E, the stock trades at 22.6×, the bottom of the 22–30× IT band, with forward P/E of 17.1×, EV/EBITDA of 14.8× (P25 vs the broad market) and price at 15.7% of its 52-week range, so I grade it fair-to-cheap and call it fair. The biggest risk is that headline growth stays in single digits while the founder CMD, Diwakar Nigam, remains unavailable due to ill-health. That combines with next-FY EPS estimate cuts (-2.5% over 90 days) and middling cash conversion (CFO/PAT 0.72×).

fundamental.thesis: Sagility is a mid-cap healthcare outsourcing company. About 90% of revenue comes from US health insurers (payers) and about 10% from hospitals and other providers. Adani Energy Solutions is India's largest private power-transmission company, with about 30% market share, plus the Mumbai distribution business and a fast-growing smart-meter platform, which together form a regulated-asset compounder funded by heavy borrowing. H1 FY27 revenue rose 47.5% YoY to ₹19,787 cr and PAT rose 137% to ₹2,600 cr; backing out Q1 (₹9,711 cr revenue, ₹1,149 cr PAT) gives an implied Q2 of about ₹10,076 cr revenue (about +53% YoY) and ₹1,451 cr PAT (about 14.4% margin), so growth is accelerating and margins are improving. However, part of the revenue jump is low-margin Mumbai distribution pass-through, and earlier-period figures are internally inconsistent (9M FY26 revenue exceeds full-year FY26). On the capital-intensive yardstick the sector card favours, EV/EBITDA of 25.1x is far above what regulated utility annuities typically command, and P/B of 7.2x against ROE of only 9.7% plus a trailing P/E of 81.7x (P88 vs the broad market) make the stock expensive even after allowing for strong growth, rising sell-side estimates (FY EPS +16% over 30 days) and the price sitting near its 52-week high (89.5% of range). fundamental.thesis: SJVN is a government-owned regulated hydropower IPP (flagship 1,500 MW Nathpa Jhakri complex) expanding aggressively into renewables and thermal (Buxar 1,320 MW), earning a CERC-regulated ROE on commissioned capacity — earnings growth is therefore a function of commissioning pace, not power prices. Q1FY27 revenue surged +52% YoY to ₹1,394 cr driven by capacity additions, but PAT fell 1.2% to ₹225 cr as PAT margin compressed severely from 24.8% to 16.1% — a pattern that has deteriorated every quarter for six periods, with EBITDA margin also contracting from ~88% to 66%, reflecting rising interest burden on a highly leveraged balance sheet (D/E 2.25×, DSCR 0.60 — a 40% shortfall in debt servicing). Using EV/EBITDA as the primary yardstick for a capital-intensive regulated utility, at 15.88× SJVN sits within the regulated-utility peer range and at P28 vs broad market, while P/B at 1.86× (P16 vs peers) and forward P/E at 14× (P22 vs peers, deep discount to trailing 38×) reflect market pricing in earnings recovery — grading overall as fair, but the 52-week position at 12.8% of range and ongoing sell-side EPS cuts of -13.3% over 30 days caution against treating the cheapness as a catalyst. The DSCR of 0.60 combined with a current ratio of 0.54 means near-term liquidity is structurally stressed, and the NJHPS tariff determination pending since April 2024 (₹3,200+ cr billed provisionally under an expired 2019 tariff) creates a binary earnings event with no resolution timeline visible.

Using EV/EBITDA as the primary yardstick for this capital-intensive business (per sector card instruction), 15.03× vs a broad-market median of 23.3× places TORNTPOWER at the P25 cheapness rank; the trailing P/E of 30.25× sits above the 10–18× utility sector benchmark, but the forward P/E compressing to 23.1× signals the market is already pricing in earnings recovery from the commissioning pipeline, yielding a fair overall valuation grade. The CFO resignation (August 2026) is a governance red flag at a sensitive execution juncture for a midcap, compounded by elevated leverage from Nabha and LNG supply disruptions already suppressing thermal plant performance.

Adani Total Gas is a city gas distributor selling CNG to vehicles and piped gas to homes and industry, a regulated volume business that is closer to a utility than to an oil company. In the latest quarter with official filings (Q1FY27; the Q2FY27 results PDF filed 2026-10-22 has not yet been extracted), revenue grew +27.2% YoY to ₹1,907 cr, faster than the roughly +17–21% of FY26, but PAT fell -14.2% to ₹142 cr. PAT margin compressed from 11.0% in Q1FY26 to 7.4%, and EBITDA margin dropped from about 19–20% to 11.2%, so the company is selling more gas but keeping much less of each rupee, which points to higher gas sourcing costs not being passed on to customers. On EV/EBITDA, the right yardstick for this capital-intensive business, the stock trades at 58.9× against a 23.3× median (P93, though the comparison set is the broad market, not tight peers), and trailing P/E of 105× is far above the 10–18× Utilities and 8–14× Energy ranges, so it is expensive even at 33% of its 52-week range. The biggest risk is that elevated LNG costs, with crude above $100 and a weak rupee, keep squeezing margins while the valuation still assumes strong earnings growth, compounded by Adani-group governance perception risk and a midcap's thinner liquidity.

fundamental.thesis: HINDPETRO is a state-run oil marketing and refining company whose earnings depend mainly on the gap between crude costs and government-influenced retail fuel and LPG prices. Q2FY27 revenue was about ₹1,39,213 cr (H1 ₹2,84,339 cr minus Q1 ₹1,45,126 cr), up roughly 26% YoY from ₹1,10,323 cr, but this growth comes from higher prices rather than profit: Q2 PAT recovered to ₹3,625 cr (2.6% margin, partly helped by ₹3,960 cr of H1 LPG compensation) after a Q1 loss of ₹12,265 cr, leaving H1 at a ₹8,639 cr loss and H1 EBITDA margin at -1.9% versus about 6.7% a year earlier. Using P/E plus dividend yield and EV/EBITDA, the yardstick the sector card sets for OMCs, the headline 4.7x trailing P/E and 4.2x EV/EBITDA look like the cheapest in the market, but they are stale: they reflect FY26 PAT of ₹18,047 cr, while actual trailing-four-quarter PAT is only about ₹1,200 cr (roughly 70x). The 7.3x forward P/E is therefore better read as policy-priced and fair, not cheap. fundamental.thesis: ITI Limited is a Government of India-owned telecom equipment manufacturer (PSU under Department of Telecommunications) engaged in defence communication, broadband gear, and telecom network products — a structurally impaired business currently in a BIFR-supervised revival plan, NOT a telecom service operator and therefore the Telecom sector card (ARPU/EBITDA framework) does not apply here. Revenue declined -14.6% YoY in Q1 FY27 (₹425 cr vs ₹498 cr), continuing a severe multi-quarter deceleration that saw -39.5% over 9MFY26 and -32.2% over H1FY26; PAT remains deeply negative at -₹32 cr (-7.4% margin), though marginally better than -₹64 cr a year ago — the 'PAT margin expanding' trajectory signal is misleading as it simply reflects a slightly smaller loss on a shrinking revenue base. Valuation is strikingly expensive: trailing P/E of 79.4× sits at P87 among 473 broad-market peers (+126% premium to market median of 35.2×) and EV/EBITDA of 483× is economically meaningless for a loss-making entity — the ₹25,371 cr market cap is pricing in the ₹8,280 cr ASCON Phase IV defence order optionality and GoI backing, not current earnings power. The single biggest risk is the material audit qualification — auditors issued a disclaimer of opinion citing Ind AS 115 revenue recognition failures on complex engineering contracts, inventory obsolescence, and inadequate internal controls, which means reported numbers cannot be relied upon and could be restated downward.

RailTel is a state-owned railway telecom and IT-infrastructure company; its legacy telecom services business, which leases the railway fibre network, is now outgrown by lower-margin government project work, so the mobile-telecom sector card (ARPU, oligopoly) does not really apply. For H1 FY27, revenue grew 20.3% YoY to ₹2,039 cr from ₹1,695 cr, but PAT fell 5.5% to ₹134 cr and PAT margin compressed from 8.2% to 6.6%, continuing a slide from 8.9% in Q1 FY26 and 7.8% in 9M FY26. Revenue growth has also cooled from +33% to about +20%, and H1 PBT included ₹39 cr of exceptional items (vs ₹13 cr a year ago), so underlying profit quality is weaker than the headline. On valuation I used EV/EBITDA plus peer rank, not the card's 9-12x mobile-telecom band: 15.3x EV/EBITDA (P27 vs a broad-market median of 23.3x) and 32.6x trailing P/E (P46, near the median) grade it fair, and the forward P/E of 21.6x assumes an earnings recovery that the falling sell-side estimates (-3% over 90 days, 2 of 2 analysts at sell) do not yet support. The biggest risk is cash conversion: H1 operating cash flow was -₹42 cr and free cash flow -₹202 cr, so growth is being bought with working capital and capex rather than producing cash.

H1 FY26 was even weaker (revenue -89.4% YoY, PAT margin -108%), so the 'accelerating/expanding' trajectory labels actually mean deeper declines and widening losses. Aditya Birla Real Estate (ABREL) is a mid-cap residential developer, operating through Birla Estates, that is moving away from its legacy pulp and paper business; it is expanding in MMR, NCR, Bengaluru and Pune, including the premium Pune projects announced on 2026-10-23. The latest extracted official quarter is Q1 FY27: total revenue rose 30.6% YoY to ₹205.7 cr, reversing the -43.0% fall in Q2 FY26, but continuing operations lost ₹67.0 cr after tax versus a ₹47.3 cr loss a year earlier, with a real-estate segment margin of -37%. Reported profit was propped up only by ₹32.4 cr from the discontinued paper business, and the Q2 FY27 results filed on 2026-10-26 have not yet been extracted, so the yfinance Q2 print (₹524 cr revenue, ₹83 cr PAT) cannot be verified. The sector card says developers should be judged on pre-sales, collections, net debt and launch pipeline rather than P/E, but none of these figures are in today's data; on the fallback yardstick the stock trades at 3.9x book with a negative ROE of -8.9% and near the bottom of its 52-week range (17%), which I grade fair rather than cheap until booking momentum can be checked. The biggest risks are a core business that keeps losing money while debt is elevated, and inconsistent balance-sheet data: reported debt-to-equity ranges from 1.57x to 5.76x, and ₹3,718 cr of preference shares need clarification.

rules.eligible: growth == strong, risk != high, data_quality != poor, revenue growth not decelerating (newest results period's YoY revenue growth >= the preceding period's, from the filing extracts; a missing number passes)
rules.rank: revenue acceleration (highest first), then revenue growth, then symbol
rules.entry: next open, once the newest results filing is >= 5 sessions old; skipped when up > 5% over 5 sessions; slots freed by sells are refilled from the eligible list the same session
rules.hold: re-judged every session on the latest view (refreshed on each results filing); topped up toward target when below 75% of target and cash allows (anti-chase applies; entries are funded first); re-qualification review every 120 sessions since entry (then since the last review): must still pass growth == strong, risk != high, revenue growth not decelerating (a missing number passes), else sold — a name failing the gate but not deteriorated is sold only at this review, never earlier
rules.exit: growth -> weak, risk -> high, sentiment bearish with conviction >= 0.5, or the 120-session review failing (growth not strong, risk high or decelerating); between reviews never for decelerating, never for timing, never on missing data
rules.overlay: target exposure 1.0 above / 0.5 below the equal-weight large-cap proxy's 200-day SMA (state confirmed over 5 consecutive sessions), applied to the whole book: every target weight is exposure/N and holdings are rebalanced toward it on the session the state flips (band +/-25%); this book trims on the flip down and tops up any session

rules.entry: next open; skipped when up > 5% over 5 sessions (no results-timing leg); slots freed by sells are refilled the same session
rules.hold: re-judged every session on the latest view (refreshed on each results filing); topped up toward target when below 75% of target and cash allows (anti-chase applies; entries are funded first); re-qualification review every 120 sessions since entry (then since the last review): must still pass growth in {strong, moderate}, risk != high, conviction >= 0.5 (rule (a) without the data-quality leg), else sold — a name failing the gate but not deteriorated is sold only at this review, never earlier
rules.exit: growth -> weak, risk -> high, sentiment bearish with conviction >= 0.5, or the 120-session review failing (rule (a) no longer met); between reviews never for decelerating, never for timing, never on missing data
rules.overlay: target exposure 1.0 above / 0.5 below the equal-weight large-cap proxy's 200-day SMA (state confirmed over 5 consecutive sessions), applied to the whole book: every target weight is exposure/N and holdings are rebalanced toward it on the session the state flips (band +/-25%); this book trims on the flip down and tops up any session
rules.review_gate: growth in {strong, moderate}, risk != high, conviction >= 0.5

books.title: Book 6 bottom-up, neutral tilts (no model)
books.hypothesis: Book 6's construction with every sector tilt at 1.0, run live beside Book 6: the line the model tilt must beat by more than the random band (the bounds study of 26 Oct 2026 found no pack field beat it; the TWR line cannot judge the tilt, Book 6 − b6_neutral and the sector-call scorecard can).

rules.signal: monthly signal date recorded (rebalance cadence); NO sector_strategist call
rules.tilt: 1.0 for every sector, always (neutral = equal share over the sectors with eligible names or a holding)
rules.eligible: the shared fundamental filter: growth == strong, risk != high, data_quality != poor, revenue growth not decelerating (newest results period's YoY revenue growth >= the preceding period's, from the filing extracts; a missing number passes); ranked by revenue acceleration (highest first), then revenue growth, then symbol
rules.slots: 30 slots apportioned over the active sectors by largest remainder on w_s x 30 (sum = 30 exactly), with hysteresis: a sector's count changes only when its exact share moves > 0.5 slot from its current allocation; weight w_s / k_s each, capped at 2/30
rules.overlay: target exposure 1.0 above / 0.5 below the equal-weight large-cap proxy's 200-day SMA (state confirmed over 5 consecutive sessions), applied to the whole book: every target weight is exposure/N and holdings are rebalanced toward it on the session the state flips (band +/-25%); rebalanced on the monthly signal date and on the flip
rules.entry: next open, once the newest results filing is >= 5 sessions old; skipped when up > 5% over 5 sessions or exited in the last 20 sessions
rules.exit: fundamental deterioration (growth -> weak / risk -> high), or a tilt cut dropping k_s below the names held (lowest-ranked sold first); never on missing data, decelerating growth or timing
rules.rebalance: signal dates and the session the overlay flips; survivors outside +/-25% of target
rules.attribution: monthly Brinson vs the equal-weight universe (leaderboard key b6_neutral_attribution); no sector calls, so no scorecard
rules.judge: the comparator for Book 6: Book 6 − b6_neutral is the tilt's contribution

books.title: Growth screen (ranked by PAT growth)
books.hypothesis: Avoid what the grades call losers (high risk, weak growth, poor data, decelerating), then buy the highest reported revenue growth — the one fundamental the winners forensic found on the winners' side — with Book 3's construction.

rules.eligible: risk != high, growth != weak, data_quality != poor, revenue growth not decelerating (a missing number passes), revenue growth YoY > 0 (newest results period with a number; missing fails)
rules.rank: PAT growth YoY from the filings, highest first (missing last), then revenue growth, then symbol
rules.entry: next open, once the newest results filing is >= 5 sessions old; skipped when up > 5% over 5 sessions; slots freed by sells are refilled from the eligible list the same session
rules.hold: re-judged every session on the latest view (refreshed on each results filing); topped up toward target when below 75% of target and cash allows (anti-chase applies; entries are funded first); re-qualification review every 120 sessions since entry (then since the last review): must still pass the same filter, else sold — a name failing the gate but not deteriorated is sold only at this review, never earlier
rules.exit: growth -> weak, risk -> high, or the 120-session review failing (the same filter); no sentiment exit
rules.overlay: target exposure 1.0 above / 0.5 below the equal-weight large-cap proxy's 200-day SMA (state confirmed over 5 consecutive sessions), applied to the whole book: every target weight is exposure/N and holdings are rebalanced toward it on the session the state flips (band +/-25%); this book trims on the flip down and tops up any session
rules.review_gate: risk != high, growth != weak, data_quality != poor, revenue growth not decelerating (a missing number passes), revenue growth YoY > 0 (newest results period with a number; missing fails)

books.kill_rule: more than 10 points behind the equal-weight null on a rolling 60-date basis, twice in a row
books.promote_rule: best book at 90 dates, if ahead of both benchmarks

brinson.method: Brinson-Fachler vs the equal-weight universe, start-of-month holdings held through the month; Cash is a sector with zero return and zero benchmark weight
